title: Worst to First: The Commissioner Who Finally Earned His Own Trophy Page
body: Sonny built this league and its website, and for two years the site's history page was not kind to its architect. Ben Dover went 6-8 in Buckaroo Bowl I's 2023 season, scored 1,413.3 points, snuck in as the 5 seed, and still slid all the way down the consolation ladder to sixth of six. It was a respectable losing record that ended in a disrespectful place, and it set the tone for what came next.

Then came 2024, the low point of the franchise. Ben Dover went 5-9, scored just 1,304.3 points, landed the 6 seed, and finished last again. The tell was on the waiver wire: Sonny made exactly one pickup all season, a hands-off approach that would be generous to call strategic. The bottom came in week 12, when he put up 44.1 points against Mekhi, still the worst week of his career.

In 2025 the commissioner stopped watching and started managing. He made 22 pickups, swung his first-ever trade, and rode Ben Dover to a 13-3 record, 1,850.8 points, and the 1 seed. The peak was a 153.4-point eruption against Randy in week 10, his best week ever, and a perfect 1-0 playoff run ended with the Buckaroo Bowl III title. Two last places to a championship is the cleanest worst-to-first arc this league has, and the guy who controls the website gets to read about it every time he logs in.

The head-to-head ledger shows a manager who beats most of the room. He's 7-5 against both Ramon and Mekhi, 6-5 against Alan, and 5-3 against Randy, who will remember that 153-point afternoon. The one rival with the edge is Kaushal, the two-time champ who leads the series 6-5. He's 1-0 against Jordan and 0-1 against Zoe, which means the rookie took down the reigning champion on her first try.

Now running The Horse is Hea, Sonny has kept the 2025 habits. He's 5-2 with 853.6 points, has already made two trades and 17 pickups, and holds 28% title odds. Somewhere between Chicago and his new Boston life he picked up a taste for winning, and the rest of the league would love to know whether it's the accent or the waiver claims. The defending champ is still very much in it.
